answers.answer: In the 3-player case, the tied leaders gain no coin and the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Census: tied lead gives no coin; unique last pays 1; in a 2-player game the last player never pays.

answers.answer: No. Draw at most the allowance and no more than the two free Market spaces. Any Market Followers left unused remain there between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Draw any number up to Knights Track allowance, limited by free Market spaces; unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds, but cannot execute it until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs one of two). A fully activated action can be saved. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology remains in place.
answers.evidence: Planning: fill gradually; activation only when all required spaces are occupied; activation can be saved. Actions: return Followers used for ordinary action to bag; Technology stays.

answers.answer: Starting with Start Player, players go clockwise repeatedly, taking one activated action or passing. Passing ends your participation for the Action Phase. Any unused activation retains its Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Actions: one activated action or passing per turn; passing ends participation; unused activations keep their Followers on the board.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted on that space.
answers.evidence: Farm House: Put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.

answers.answer: Village chooses one recruit: Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader; each goes into your bag and advances its profession track. Boatman gives the depicted coins (or a Citizen to the first player at the last space); Craftsman gives a Technology tile; Trader gives a Place Tile, category I on the first advance and I or II on later advances.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment bullets: Boatman coins/Citizen; Craftsman Technology; Trader Place Tile and category rules.

answers.answer: No. A newly acquired Technology can only be used after you pass, so it cannot help another action that round after that pass. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. Never place more than one at a Place or one at a Place requiring only one Follower; later tiles can replace any profession except Monk. Technology stays and cannot be moved.
answers.evidence: Craftsman-acquired tile is used only after passing. Technology: first must replace Farmer; later any except Monk; no more than one at a Place or at a one-Follower Place; cannot be moved.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only. Every later advance permits I or II. Players may inspect the stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Setup: players may inspect stacks at any time. Trader: first advance permits category I only; every later advance allows I or II.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances Scholars Track, and grants its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances Knights Track; the fourth Knight leaves the draw allowance at 7, and its Citizen goes to the first player there. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. Once a character track is at its last space, that action cannot be taken again.
answers.evidence: Actions table and Castle rewards; Character-track limits.

answers.answer: Yes, a Monk can replace a Knight for an ordinary action. No Knight or Technology can replace a required Monk. No, Deed spaces require exact professions and substitutions cannot replace those professions.
answers.evidence: Monks: can replace any other profession on ordinary actions; reverse forbidden. Deeds: substitutions cannot replace exact professions depicted.

answers.answer: One Ship or Wagon action moves the Merchant one connection to an adjacent town (Waterway for Ship, Road for Wagon). You may take at most one good from that connection, even if two lie there. Empty connections are legal and yield no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: one connection; one good, choosing one if several; empty Roads/Waterways legal and yield no good.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the Merchant's current town. A town with any player's station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building: Merchant in town; town with any station cannot receive another; Orléans exception.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gains 1 Development Point. Moving onto or past a coin space collects its depicted coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Scriptorium action gives 1 Development Point; Scoring: moving onto or past coin/Citizen/status spaces gives the stated rewards/Status change.

answers.answer: Town Hall works with one or two eligible Followers; marked starting Followers cannot be used. Send one or both permanently to free Deed spaces matching their exact professions, possibly on different Deeds. Each placement grants its depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; Canalization offers 1 coin or 1 Development Point. Whoever fills a Deed's last space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: one or two neutral Followers; exact profession; rewards and Citizen for filling last space.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5 (the Action Phase), so it applies before the Event Phase. Other events resolve in Phase 6. The stack is arranged so round 1 always has Pilgrimage.
answers.evidence: Hour Glass: Pilgrimage instead prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5; Phase 6 resolves events. Setup puts Pilgrimage on top.

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine count as food; wool and brocade do not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you cannot pay food, pay 5 coins; if unable to pay those coins, undergo torture for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Harvest: Pay one grain, cheese, or wine to Goods Market; if unable pay 5 coins; if unable to pay coins, torture. Wool and brocade are not food.

answers.answer: A neutral Scholar returns to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. A marked starting Trader is kept, causes no Follower loss that round, and is not redrawn.
answers.evidence: Plague: neutral returns to supply, do not move track; marked starting Follower keep it, lose no Follower, do not redraw.

answers.answer: Pay the one available coin, then replace each of the two missing coins with an item or mix of items: a built or unbuilt Trading Station, one eligible random neutral Follower, one Development Point moved left (never onto or past a coin space), one Goods Tile, Place Tile, or Technology tile. Marked starting Followers are redrawn until an eligible neutral is found. Surrendered items are removed from the game. The summary does not specify any special choice constraint beyond the listed eligible items and the one-item-per-missing-coin rule.
answers.evidence: Torture: pay available coins and replace each missing coin with one item from any mix; starting Followers redrawn; items removed; Development Point restriction.

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods Tile, even if another part would still give a reward. It becomes available again when the required tile returns to availability, subject to usual requirements. If common supply has too few coins, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies: cannot play an action providing an unavailable tile; becomes available when required tile is available; insufficient coin supply means no coins received then.

answers.answer: A tie for most built stations means nobody takes the bonus Citizen. Goods score grain/cheese/wine/wool/brocade at 1/2/3/4/5 points each. Stations plus collected Citizens score (number of built stations + number of Citizens) × final Development Status. A final-score tie goes to the player furthest ahead on Development Track; if still tied, they share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions: unique most gets Citizen; tie nobody; goods values; formula; tie-break.

answers.answer: Each player gets a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Starting Followers go on the Market; Merchant goes in Orléans; one marker goes on the first space of each six Character Tracks and the Development Track; coins and unbuilt stations stay in front of the player. The youngest player takes Start Player token.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2 and final sentence.

answers.answer: Place 13 Citizens on marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for final Trading Station award. Sort neutral Followers by profession into their buildings; set Technology in supply. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II, with stacks inspectable. For four players, shuffle goods face down and deal one face up on every eligible Road/Waterway goods space; sort remaining goods face up into Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, 5; Fewer players says in 4-player games fill every such space.

answers.answer: For 3 players remove 2 neutral each of Farmer, Boatman, Craftsman, Trader; remove 3 each of Knight, Scholar, Monk; remove 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players remove 4 of each first group; 6 each of Knight, Scholar, Monk; remove 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and sentence above it.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table required Followers column.

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table required Followers column.

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall accepts one or two eligible neutral Followers; starting marked Followers are excluded. Its Deed destinations require exact matching professions.
answers.evidence: Actions table; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Yes. For each of two declined draws, you may return one Follower from an Action Space to your Market. You cannot move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: For each draw declined, may move one Follower from an Action Space back to Market; this is permitted recovery method.

answers.answer: Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but must shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Followers phase: may inspect bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.

answers.answer: The phases are Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass the Start Player token left. Begin planning simultaneously and announce completion; if order matters, plan clockwise from Start Player. Payments and any order-sensitive event resolution proceed clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases 1–7; Planning and Event details.

answers.answer: Finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including its event; scoring follows after that round.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions: Finish the entire round in which the 18th tile is drawn, including its event. Before scoring…

answers.answer: The player uniquely ahead on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin, regardless of how many Farmer tiles are in bags.
answers.evidence: Census compares Farmers Track markers regardless of Farmer tiles currently in bags.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events: Income — Gain coins equal to Development Status.

answers.answer: With eight goods, pay 2 coins (one per complete group of three, rounding down). Types do not change the count; count all goods. A shortfall causes torture.
answers.evidence: Taxes: count all goods; pay 1 coin per complete group of 3 (round down); shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: Receive 4 coins, one per built Trading Station. Unbuilt stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Trading Day gives 1 coin per built Trading Station; only built stations count.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer, takes 1 grain; Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer, takes 1 cheese; Winery: Farmer + Trader, takes 1 wine; Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader, takes 1 wool; Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader, takes 1 brocade. All take the good from Goods Market, and a goods-producing Place cannot be used if that particular good is absent there.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table and goods-availability rule.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman, gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk, gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman, gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar, gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins and advance one Development space per coin; paying two advances two spaces. Zero and four coins are not allowed.
answers.evidence: Pharmacy: Any 1 Follower; pay 1–3; one space per coin; must spend at least 1 and no more than 3.

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar, gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, gain one coin per Trading Station built. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, gain coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight; it moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table: Horse Wagon.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile. Your first ever Technology cannot be placed on Laboratory because it must replace a Farmer. A later one may be placed on either of its spaces if none is already there and usual constraints are met.
answers.evidence: Laboratory entry and first-Technology Farmer rule.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces; none can go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse: Farmer; draw 3, choose 2; place immediately; none on Bathhouse; return third and activating Follower.

answers.answer: Place the one Follower that can legally go on an allowed Action Space. Return all other drawn Followers and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Follower.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse: If can legally place only one or none, do so and return all other drawn Followers to bag.

answers.answer: It may be executed later this round on one of your action turns, as long as you have not passed. You choose your actions' order freely; passing ends participation.
answers.evidence: Actions: choose actions' order freely; one activated action or pass per turn; passing ends participation.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague.
answers.evidence: Sacristy entry: activated protection during Phase 6 against negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, Plague; return Monk to bag.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5, before the Sacristy's protection is used in Phase 6. The Phase 6 protection therefore cannot undo the recruitment restriction.
answers.evidence: Pilgrimage applies in Phase 5; Sacristy protection is used during Phase 6.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not permit replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: Herb Garden: Boatmen may replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It has no activation cost. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: School: No activation; Scholars may replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions.

answers.answer: No. Beneficial Deed spaces require exact professions; substitutions cannot fill a differently depicted Deed space. Using Gunpowder Tower instead of Town Hall does not change the exact-profession rule.
answers.evidence: Beneficial Deeds require exact professions; Town Hall section says substitutions cannot replace Deed professions; Gunpowder Tower says Deed spaces still require exact types.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds two Market spaces. During Phase 3, put one or two drawn Followers there. In Planning, move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, during Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent; Deeds require exact types.
answers.evidence: Gunpowder Tower entry.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two tied furthest behind pay nothing because tied last place pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Census: unique leader gains 1; tied last place pays nothing.

answers.answer: The unique leader in built Trading Stations receives the set-aside Citizen after the entire round in which tile 18 is revealed, before scoring. That Citizen counts among collected Citizens in final station/Citizen scoring.
answers.evidence: Finish entire round 18 including event; before scoring unique most built stations takes set-aside Citizen; formula includes collected Citizens.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, and put Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1 the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup: remove lighter Pilgrimage, shuffle other 17, put Pilgrimage on top. Phase 1: Start Player reveals top tile.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring table: Coins — 1 each.

answers.answer: Initial Development Status is 1 and initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup: Development Status starts at 1; initial draw allowance is 4.

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, stations, Places, and Technology are removed from the game rather than returned to supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture: surrendered items are removed from game; only lost Development Points can be regained.

answers.answer: You may choose the execution order freely.
answers.evidence: Actions: Choose your actions' order freely.

answers.answer: It is available immediately, including during the current Action Phase.
answers.evidence: Trader recruitment: acquired Place and passive special ability are available immediately, including current Action Phase.

answers.answer: You may send just one or both; you are not required to send both.
answers.evidence: Town Hall action sends one or both Followers.

answers.answer: You may leave the good there; the summary says you may take one good, not that taking it is mandatory.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: you may take one good from that connection; empty connections are legal.

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the two Town Hall Followers in separate action turns during the same Action Phase before passing.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Town Hall Followers may be sent in separate action turns during same Action Phase before passing.
